title: Chicken Piccata
subtitle: Pan-fried chicken with lemon and caper butter sauce
excerpt: This is a sharp, bright pan sauce that takes about five minutes to come together once the chicken is cooked. The capers give a briny hit and the butter at the end gives the sauce its gloss and body.
sourceNotes: Piccata is an Italian-American technique applied most often to veal or chicken, derived from the Italian piccata meaning larded. The sauce of lemon, capers, and butter became a restaurant staple across the United States through the mid twentieth century.

content.text: Have the butter cut into small cubes and kept cold. Adding it off the heat in two stages is what makes the sauce shiny and emulsified rather than greasy.

items.prepNote: cut into small cubes, kept cold
juice of both, zest of one

content.text: Flatten the chicken breasts to about 1 cm. Season and dust lightly in flour, shaking off the excess.
Heat 1 tbsp of butter with the olive oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken in batches for 3-4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Remove and rest on a plate.
Pour off any excess oil. Add the garlic to the pan and cook for 30 seconds over medium heat. Add the chicken stock and lemon juice, scraping up the browned bits. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the capers and lemon zest. Reduce the heat to low and swirl in the remaining cold butter a cube at a time, moving the pan as you go, until the sauce is glossy and slightly thickened.
Return the chicken to the pan and spoon sauce over the top. Scatter with parsley and serve immediately.

items.cause: Butter added when the pan was too hot.
items.fix: Remove the pan from the heat and let it cool for 30 seconds before adding butter. Swirl constantly and do not rush.
